origin: Own anonymous two-conformation pulling model; all energies, extensions, transition rates and protocol choices below are stipulated mathematical quantities, not experimental observations or properties of a named biomolecule.
states_and_units: States F=0 and U=1 have extensions0 and1. At force f their energies are E_F(f)=0 and E_U(f)=3-f. Set beta=1, so all work and free energies are in kBT units; natural logarithms are used throughout. Equilibrium probabilities at force f are proportional to exp(-E_s(f)). Row-vector convention is mandatory: p(t)=p(0)exp(tQ_f). At each fixed force, rates F->U=a_f=1/(1+exp(3-f)), U->F=b_f=1-a_f; Q_f=[[-a_f,a_f],[b_f,-b_f]]. Thus the total relaxation rate is1 and detailed balance holds. An instantaneous force quench changes energy but never the state.
bounded_protocol: Forward runs start in equilibrium at f=0. Quench0->1, hold f=1 for tau, quench1->3, hold f=3 for2-tau, then quench3->4 and stop immediately. The design domain is the CLOSED interval0<=tau<=2. No relaxation at the final force is added. Define s0,s1,s2 as the states at the three quenches, in chronological order; a trajectory is one of the eight binary triples in lexicographic order000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111. Work done ON the molecule is the sum of its energy changes at the three quenches only; heat during holds is not work. Repeated work values from distinct trajectories must be aggregated, not arbitrarily deduplicated.
reverse_experiment: For every fixed tau the true reverse starts from equilibrium at f=4, quenches4->3, holds at3 for2-tau, quenches3->1, holds at1 for tau, then quenches1->0. Reverse state triples are indexed in THEIR chronological order. To compare path laws, pair forward(s0,s1,s2) with reverse(s2,s1,s0). The paired reverse work is the negative forward work. Changing the initial distribution or keeping the forward hold order is a different experiment. Derive the complete path likelihood ratio from equilibrium endpoints and detailed balance, and establish the exponential work identity for every allowed tau, including zero-duration holds.
objectives: Compare two protocol objectives over the whole closed design interval: (i) minimize mean dissipated work <W>-DeltaF; (ii) minimize the leading large-N variance coefficient R(tau)=Var(exp(-W))/<exp(-W)>^2 of -log of the empirical exponential-work mean. This is an asymptotic variance coefficient N*Var(estimator), not a finite-N mean-square error or the variance of W itself. Express <W> and <exp(-2W)> separately as alpha+beta*exp(-tau)+gamma*exp(tau), report each coefficient triple, and prove the complete global optima by signs/strict curvature and both endpoints. Retain complete registered polynomial root inventories for both stationarity equations in y=exp(tau)>0, and reject roots outside1<=y<=exp(2). A time grid or local numerical minimum does not prove globality. The public schema reports both optima, both minimum objectives and each objective evaluated at the OTHER optimum.
actual_operator_evidence: At tau=1 AND at each of the two independently selected optimal dwell values, retain actual complete registered MatrixExponential outputs for both full2x2hold generators. At every one of these three dwell choices retain the registered matrix product of the ACTUAL first-hold transition matrix with the ACTUAL second-hold transition matrix; these are unweighted state propagators, distinct from work-weighted tilted products. Use the returned complete matrices to construct all eight forward path probabilities, mean work and exponential moments, retaining complete numerical evidence. For tau1 additionally construct all eight paired reverse probabilities with the reversed hold order and equilibrium f4 endpoint, verify every individual path likelihood ratio and both normalized laws, and retain all work-bin sums. Both tau0 and tau2 must be treated using identity transitions for the vanished hold; zero-probability paths must not enter a log(0/0).
information_loss: At tau1 report KL(P_F(s0,s1,s2)||P_R(s2,s1,s0)), KL of the forward work law against the paired reverse law binned by the NEGATIVE reverse work, and KL of the forward terminal state distribution against the reverse INITIAL equilibrium at4. Establish whether either coarsening preserves all relative entropy and why; an inequality from a numerical sample alone does not establish sufficiency. Explain the relation to mean dissipation and distinguish the equilibrium endpoint free-energy difference from the actual nonequilibrium final state.
work_measurement_noise: Only in this separate detector analysis, each full-trajectory measured work is W_obs=W+eta, with eta independent of all paths and eta~N(0,1/4). Its variance is for the TOTAL work, not per quench. For iid repeats consider the estimator -log(mean(exp(-W_obs)))+1/8. Determine the large-sample limit if the +1/8 correction is OMITTED, whether the stated correction removes ALL finite-N bias, and the leading large-N bias coefficient N*(E[corrected_estimator]-DeltaF) at the variance-optimal dwell. Derive the correction and coefficient from Gaussian moments and the log expansion; this coefficient is not an exact finite-N bias. Decide whether this known independent noise changes the variance-optimal dwell. The detector noise is not a change to the physical path law or detailed balance.

interpretation_proposals.A: A dwell design that minimizes dissipation can differ from the design giving the most precise exponential-work free-energy estimator.
interpretation_proposals.B: Final forward equilibration is necessary for the finite-time exponential work identity.
interpretation_proposals.C: A likelihood ratio depending only on total work makes work sufficient for this forward/reverse discrimination, even when several paths share a work value.
interpretation_proposals.D: The work variance and the exponential-work variance define interchangeable protocol objectives.
interpretation_proposals.E: Independent unbiased work noise can bias a nonlinear exponential-work free-energy estimate.
interpretation_proposals.F: Knowing and correcting the Gaussian moment factor guarantees exact unbiasedness of the finite-sample logarithm.
interpretation_proposals.G: Reversing only the force labels while leaving the hold order unchanged is always the required reverse experiment.
interpretation_proposals.H: Endpoint probabilities, force-work signs and reversed trajectory order must be consistent before fluctuation identities can be used.

reporting: Use the public answer schema. Numeric absolute tolerance1e-7. Coefficient arrays are ordered constant, exp(-tau), exp(+tau), not polynomial descending order. Path arrays use the eight explicitly listed FORWARD triples; paired reverse array uses their reversed triples in this SAME forward index order. Work bins are ascending[-4,-3,-2,-1,0]. Final state array is[F,U]. Counts, exact work values, booleans and proposal IDs remain exact. Preserve the all-tau likelihood/global optimization and finite-sample/noise reasoning in the trajectory, together with the complete actual operator and root evidence.

primary_context.title: Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences
Entropy production fluctuation theorem and the nonequilibrium work relation for free energy differences

context_role: Primary methodological context for finite-time work identities and correctly reversed equilibrium-start experiments. This question specifies its own anonymous molecule, rates, protocol family, objectives and detector model; no article dataset, prose, figure or experimental molecule is reproduced.
